data.title: Accessory
data.definition: An article that is not itself a medical device but is intended by its manufacturer to be used together with one or more particular medical devices specifically to enable the device to be used according to its intended purpose or to specifically and directly assist its medical functionality.

data.title: Activity
data.definition: A unit of work performed by an actor or process to fulfil, assess or maintain a regulatory, quality or product obligation.

data.title: Actor Registration
data.definition: The EUDAMED registration record and process through which an economic operator obtains or maintains its actor identity, including its Single Registration Number where applicable.

data.title: Answer Pattern
data.definition: A reusable structure specifying which facts, relationships, evidence, decisions and provenance should be assembled to answer a competency question.

data.title: Article10a Assessment
data.definition: A documented assessment of whether an anticipated supply interruption or discontinuation meets the conditions that trigger notification under MDR Article 10a.

data.title: Article10a Notification
data.definition: A notification made to the relevant competent authority and affected economic operators or institutions when the conditions in MDR Article 10a are met.

data.title: Assertion
data.definition: A reviewable subject-predicate-object statement whose status, provenance, evidence and temporal validity can be recorded and evaluated.

data.title: Assessment
data.definition: A structured evaluation of defined information against stated criteria that produces a documented finding, conclusion or decision input.

data.title: Audit
data.definition: A systematic, independent and documented examination used to determine whether activities and results conform to planned arrangements and applicable requirements.

data.title: Authorised Representative
data.definition: A natural or legal person established in the EU that has received and accepted a written mandate from a manufacturer located outside the EU to act on the manufacturer's behalf in relation to specified MDR obligations.

data.title: Basic UDI Di
data.definition: The primary identifier of a device model/group used as the main key connecting devices with the same intended purpose, risk class and essential design/manufacturing characteristics. It is independent of packaging or production information and serves as a principal access key in EUDAMED.

data.title: Benefit Risk Determination
data.definition: A documented conclusion comparing the device's demonstrated benefits with its individual and overall residual risks for the intended purpose and population.

data.title: CAPA
data.definition: **Corrective and Preventive Action** system/process for investigating actual or potential quality/compliance problems, determining causes, implementing actions and verifying effectiveness.

data.title: Ce Marking State
data.definition: The controlled status describing whether and on what basis CE marking may be affixed to a device configuration.

data.title: CER
data.definition: **Clinical Evaluation Report**: the controlled report documenting the clinical evaluation, its evidence, methodology, assessment and conclusions.

data.title: Certificate
data.definition: A conformity-assessment certificate issued by a notified body where the applicable MDR conformity-assessment procedure requires certification. The ontology should record its type, scope, issuing notified body, validity and device/configuration coverage.

data.title: Certificate Registration
data.definition: The EUDAMED record representing the registration or update of a conformity-assessment certificate and its regulatory status.

data.title: Change
data.definition: A controlled modification to a product, process, supplier, document, software item or regulatory state that requires impact assessment and approval.

data.title: Change Impact Assessment
data.definition: A documented evaluation of how a proposed or implemented change affects device configuration, risk, clinical evidence, regulatory status, documentation and required actions.

data.title: Classification Decision
data.definition: The approved, traceable conclusion assigning a device class by applying relevant Annex VIII rules to controlled device facts.

data.title: Classification Rule
data.definition: A rule or sub-rule in Annex VIII used to determine a device's risk class from characteristics such as duration, invasiveness, active function, anatomical location or software function.

data.title: Clinical Claim
data.definition: A manufacturer statement about a device's clinical benefit, performance or outcome that must remain consistent with the intended purpose and supported by clinical evidence.

data.title: Clinical Evaluation
data.definition: The systematic and planned process of continuously generating, collecting, analysing and assessing clinical data relating to a device to verify safety, performance and clinical benefit when used as intended.

data.title: Clinical Evaluation Plan
data.definition: The controlled plan defining the scope, methods, data sources, appraisal criteria and outputs for clinical evaluation of a device.

data.title: Clinical Evaluation Report
data.definition: **Clinical Evaluation Report**: the controlled report documenting the clinical evaluation, its evidence, methodology, assessment and conclusions.

data.title: Clinical Evidence
data.definition: Clinical data and clinical-evaluation results pertaining to a device of sufficient amount and quality to permit a qualified assessment of whether the device is safe and achieves the intended clinical benefit when used as intended.

data.title: Clinical Investigation
data.definition: A systematic investigation involving one or more human subjects undertaken to assess the safety or performance of a medical device.

data.title: Common Specification
data.definition: A set of technical or clinical requirements, other than a standard, issued by the European Commission for devices, processes or systems under the MDR.

data.title: Comparator Device
data.definition: A device selected as a reference for clinical, performance, state-of-the-art or equivalence analysis.

data.title: Competency Question
data.definition: A question the ontology must be able to answer using explicitly represented facts, relationships, rules, evidence and provenance.

data.title: Competent Authority
data.definition: A national authority designated by a Member State to carry out functions assigned under the MDR.

data.title: Complaint
data.definition: A communication alleging a deficiency related to the identity, quality, durability, reliability, usability, safety or performance of a released device. A complaint may or may not constitute an MDR incident.

data.title: Compliance Gap
data.definition: A recorded absence, insufficiency, inconsistency or unresolved state that prevents a requirement or lifecycle gate from being demonstrated as satisfied.

data.title: Compliance Requirement Instance
data.definition: A device-, configuration-, market- and lifecycle-specific instance of a generic requirement, including applicability, responsible party, required evidence and compliance state.

data.title: Compliance State
data.definition: A controlled status expressing the evaluated condition of a requirement instance, such as satisfied, not satisfied, not applicable or unresolved.

data.title: Component
data.definition: A constituent part, material, subassembly or software element incorporated into or used by a device. A component is not automatically a separately regulated medical device.

data.title: Configuration Baseline
data.definition: An approved, uniquely identified snapshot of the product and documentation items that together define a device configuration at a point in time.

data.title: Conformity Assessment
data.definition: The process demonstrating whether the MDR requirements relating to a device have been fulfilled. Depending on device class and route, this can involve manufacturer activities and notified-body assessment.

data.title: Conformity Assessment Route
data.definition: The selected MDR conformity-assessment procedure applicable to a device, considering its class, characteristics and any notified-body involvement.

data.title: Constraint
data.definition: A machine-checkable condition that valid ontology data or a compliant product context is required to satisfy.

data.title: Contraindication
data.definition: A circumstance, condition or patient characteristic in which the device should not be used because the expected risk is unacceptable or use is inappropriate.

data.title: Controlled Vocabulary
data.definition: A governed set of permitted values and meanings used to keep ontology data consistent and machine-checkable.

data.title: Decision
data.definition: An approved conclusion selected from available alternatives on the basis of stated facts, criteria, evidence and authority.

data.title: Declaration Of Conformity
data.definition: The manufacturer's formal EU declaration stating that the applicable MDR requirements have been fulfilled for the device(s) covered. It is issued by the manufacturer after completion of the applicable conformity-assessment obligations.

data.title: Design Change
data.definition: A controlled modification to the device design, design requirements or design outputs that is evaluated for downstream safety, performance and regulatory impact.

data.title: Design Process
data.definition: The controlled process through which user needs and regulatory requirements are transformed into device design requirements, outputs, verification, validation and released design.

data.title: Device Class
data.definition: The regulatory risk class assigned under MDR Annex VIII: Class I, IIa, IIb or III. The class influences conformity-assessment route and multiple downstream obligations.

data.title: Device Configuration
data.definition: The exact controlled combination of hardware, software, materials, accessories, packaging, labelling, manufacturing baseline and intended-purpose version for which compliance is being assessed. This should normally be the principal scope of evidence and release reasoning.

data.title: Device
data.definition: An instrument, apparatus, appliance, software, implant, reagent, material or other article intended by its manufacturer for a medical purpose and meeting the MDR definition of a medical device.

data.title: Device Family
data.definition: A manufacturer-defined grouping of related devices sharing substantial design, technology, intended-purpose or regulatory characteristics. It is useful for portfolio reasoning and evidence grouping but must not be assumed to have a single universally applicable MDR legal meaning.

data.title: Device Model
data.definition: A named product design or commercial model controlled by the manufacturer. It represents a stable product identity above individual variants or configurations.

data.title: Device Registration
data.definition: The EUDAMED record and process used to register and maintain required device and UDI information.

data.title: Device Variant
data.definition: A distinguishable version of a model differing in attributes such as size, capacity, geometry, option set, intended population or presentation while remaining related to the same model.

data.title: Distributor
data.definition: A natural or legal person in the supply chain, other than the manufacturer or importer, that makes a device available on the market up until putting it into service.

data.title: Document
data.definition: A controlled information object that may have one or more identified versions and can serve as a source, record or evidence container.

data.title: Document Version
data.definition: A uniquely identified revision of a controlled document with defined status, approval, effective dates and supersession relationships.

data.title: EMDN Code
data.definition: A code from the **European Medical Device Nomenclature**, the nomenclature manufacturers use when registering medical devices in EUDAMED.

data.title: Equivalence Assessment
data.definition: A documented comparison evaluating whether clinical, technical and biological characteristics support a claim of equivalence between devices.

data.title: EU Regulation
data.definition: A binding legislative act of the European Union that is directly applicable in Member States and can serve as a legal source for requirements.

data.title: EUDAMED Module
data.definition: A functional part of EUDAMED used for a defined regulatory information domain such as actor, UDI/device, certificate or vigilance data.

data.title: Event
data.definition: A time-bounded occurrence relevant to a device, organisation, process or regulatory state that may trigger assessment or action.

data.title: Evidence Item
data.definition: A controlled piece of objective information used to support or challenge a requirement, claim, decision, risk control or compliance conclusion.

data.title: Evidence Type
data.definition: A category describing the nature and expected content of evidence required for a regulatory or quality purpose.

data.title: Evidence Update
data.definition: A controlled revision, replacement or addition that changes the evidence available for an assessment or compliance conclusion.

data.title: FSCA
data.definition: **Field Safety Corrective Action**: corrective action taken by a manufacturer for technical or medical reasons to prevent or reduce the risk of a serious incident associated with a device made available on the market.

data.title: FSN
data.definition: A communication sent by the manufacturer to users or customers concerning an FSCA. Often abbreviated **FSN**.

data.title: Gate Decision
data.definition: The approved outcome of evaluating a lifecycle gate, stating whether progression is allowed and recording any conditions or unresolved gaps.

data.title: GSPR Requirement
data.definition: A **General Safety and Performance Requirement** from MDR Annex I. GSPRs establish the safety, performance, design and information requirements devices must satisfy when applicable.

data.title: Guidance
data.definition: A non-binding interpretive or implementation source issued by an authority or recognised regulatory group.

data.title: Hardware Revision
data.definition: A controlled version of the physical design or hardware implementation included in a device configuration.

data.title: Harm
data.definition: Injury or damage to health, property or the environment resulting from a hazardous situation. In medical-device reasoning, patient or user injury is normally the primary concern.

data.title: Harmonised Standard
data.definition: A European standard cited in the Official Journal of the European Union that may confer a presumption of conformity for the requirements it covers.

data.title: Hazard
data.definition: A potential source of harm. It may originate from energy, biological material, software behaviour, mechanical conditions, usability, substances, cybersecurity or other sources.

data.title: Hazardous Situation
data.definition: A circumstance in which people, property or the environment are exposed to one or more hazards. It links a hazard to a possible harm.

data.title: Identifier
data.definition: A controlled code or value used to distinguish and reference an ontology object without treating the identifier as the object itself.

data.title: Ifu
data.definition: The manufacturer-supplied instructions for use describing the information needed to use a device safely and as intended.

data.title: Importer
data.definition: A natural or legal person established in the Union that places a device from a third country on the Union market.

data.title: Incident Assessment
data.definition: A documented evaluation determining the nature, seriousness, reportability, causal factors and required actions for a device-related incident or complaint.

data.title: Indication
data.definition: A specific medical condition, disease, state, population or clinical circumstance for which use of the device is intended. It is usually narrower than the overall intended purpose.

data.title: Intended Purpose
data.definition: The use for which the manufacturer intends the device according to information supplied by the manufacturer, including the label, IFU, promotional/sales materials and clinical evaluation. It is one of the most consequential semantic objects in the ontology.

data.title: Intended Purpose Version
data.definition: A controlled revision of the manufacturer's intended-purpose statement used to scope classification, risk, clinical evaluation and evidence.

data.title: Intended User
data.definition: The type of person expected to operate or otherwise use the device, such as healthcare professional, trained operator, patient or lay person.

data.title: Internal Evidence
data.definition: Evidence generated or controlled within the manufacturer organisation rather than obtained from an external source.

data.title: Internal Requirement
data.definition: A manufacturer-controlled requirement derived from design, quality, risk, business or process needs rather than directly from an external normative source.

data.title: Internal Source
data.definition: A manufacturer-controlled source document from which internal requirements, decisions or evidence context are derived.

data.title: Label
data.definition: Written, printed or graphic information appearing on the device, its packaging or accompanying materials to identify it and support safe use.

data.title: Labelling Change
data.definition: A controlled modification to a label, instructions for use, packaging text, symbol, translation or other manufacturer-supplied information.

data.title: Landing Page
data.definition: A navigational entry page that introduces the knowledge system and directs users to its principal views and content areas.

data.title: Legal Provision
data.definition: A traceable article, annex, paragraph or other bounded fragment of binding law from which requirements, rules or decisions may be derived.

data.title: Legal Source
data.definition: A binding legal instrument used as authoritative provenance for regulatory requirements and decisions.

data.title: Lifecycle Gate
data.definition: A defined review point at which stated evidence and compliance criteria must be evaluated before a product or process advances.

data.title: Lifecycle State
data.definition: A controlled status representing the current stage of a product, document, process or regulatory object during its lifecycle.

data.title: Management Review
data.definition: A formal review by top management of the continuing suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of the quality management system.

data.title: Manufacturer
data.definition: A natural or legal person that manufactures or fully refurbishes a device, or has a device designed, manufactured or fully refurbished, and markets it under its name or trademark. In the ontology this is the organisation that ultimately bears the MDR manufacturer obligations for the device.

data.title: Manufacturing Change
data.definition: A controlled modification to a manufacturing method, process parameter, site, equipment or production control.

data.title: Manufacturing Site
data.definition: A controlled physical facility at which manufacturing, assembly, testing, packaging, sterilisation, release or another manufacturing activity is carried out. A manufacturer may have several manufacturing sites, and outsourced sites may belong to suppliers.

data.title: Market
data.definition: A jurisdiction or geographic regulatory context in which a device is intended to be placed, supplied or maintained.

data.title: Market Release Gate
data.definition: The lifecycle gate that verifies whether a defined device configuration is ready for lawful release or placement on a specified market.

data.title: Material Specification
data.definition: A controlled definition of the identity, properties, acceptance criteria and use of a material in a device configuration.

data.title: Mdcg Guidance
data.definition: A non-binding guidance document endorsed by the Medical Device Coordination Group to support consistent interpretation or implementation of medical-device legislation.

data.title: Meta Page
data.definition: A project-governance page explaining the ontology's modelling conventions, maintenance approach or use.

data.title: No Action Decision
data.definition: A documented decision that no corrective, preventive, regulatory or product action is required, including the evidence and rationale supporting that conclusion.

data.title: Notified Body Application
data.definition: A manufacturer's formal application to a notified body for an MDR conformity-assessment activity, with defined device and procedure scope.

data.title: Notified Body
data.definition: A conformity-assessment body designated under the MDR to perform specified third-party assessment activities.

data.title: Ontology Class
data.definition: A governed category of entities sharing a defined meaning and role in the ontology.

data.title: Organisation
data.definition: A legal, administrative or operational body represented as an actor, owner or responsible party in the manufacturer compliance system.

data.title: Packaging Configuration
data.definition: The controlled combination of packaging levels, materials, labels and presentation associated with a device configuration.

data.title: Person
data.definition: An individual represented because they perform a role, hold responsibility or participate in a regulatory or quality activity.

data.title: Pmcf Plan
data.definition: The controlled plan for proactively collecting and evaluating clinical data from use of a CE-marked device within its intended purpose.

data.title: Pmcf Report
data.definition: A report documenting results and conclusions of post-market clinical follow-up activities and the implications for clinical evaluation, risk management and other post-market activities.

data.title: Pmcf Result
data.definition: A discrete finding or conclusion produced by a post-market clinical follow-up activity.

data.title: PMS Data
data.definition: A collected post-market data item or dataset concerning device quality, performance, safety, use or market experience.

data.title: PMS Data Source
data.definition: A defined origin of post-market information, such as complaints, vigilance reports, literature, registries, surveys or service data.

data.title: PMS Finding
data.definition: A documented observation or conclusion resulting from analysis of post-market surveillance data.

data.title: PMS Plan
data.definition: The documented plan defining how the manufacturer will proactively collect and evaluate post-market information for a device.

data.title: PMS Report
data.definition: A post-market surveillance report for Class I devices summarising results and conclusions from PMS data and describing preventive and corrective actions taken.

data.title: PMS System
data.definition: The manufacturer-managed system of processes, responsibilities and records used to plan, collect, analyse and act on post-market surveillance information.

data.title: Process
data.definition: A controlled set of related activities that transforms inputs into defined outputs under assigned responsibilities and controls.

data.title: Production Process
data.definition: The controlled set of manufacturing activities that transform approved inputs/components into the finished device, including relevant process controls and validation.

data.title: Production Unit
data.definition: An individual manufactured item, batch, lot or other production-level object to which production identifiers and records may apply.

data.title: PRRC
data.definition: **Person Responsible for Regulatory Compliance**. The qualified person whose availability the manufacturer must ensure under Article 15 and to whom specified regulatory-compliance responsibilities are assigned.

data.title: PSUR
data.definition: **Periodic Safety Update Report**. For specified device classes, the manufacturer summarizes PMS results and conclusions, including benefit-risk conclusions, PMCF findings, sales/use information and population characteristics, and updates it at the applicable MDR frequency.

data.title: QMS Process
data.definition: A controlled process operating within the quality management system with defined inputs, outputs, ownership, controls and records.

data.title: QMS
data.definition: The organisational structure, responsibilities, procedures, processes and resources used to implement quality management and meet applicable regulatory requirements.

data.title: Record Type
data.definition: A governed category specifying the expected purpose, content and retention context of a record.

data.title: Registration State
data.definition: A controlled status indicating the current condition of an actor, device, certificate or submission registration.

data.title: Regulatory Change
data.definition: A controlled change to an applicable law, guidance, standard, registration, certificate or regulatory interpretation that may affect the device or QMS.

data.title: Regulatory Requirement
data.definition: Any obligation, condition or required state derived from legislation, implementing/delegated legislation or another applicable regulatory source. A GSPR is one kind of RegulatoryRequirement.

data.title: Relation Definition
data.definition: The governed contract for an ontology predicate, including its label, domain, range and logical or provenance constraints.

data.title: Release Process
data.definition: The controlled decision process confirming that a finished device/configuration satisfies defined manufacturing, quality and regulatory prerequisites before release or placement on the market.

data.title: Requirement
data.definition: A stated need, obligation or condition that a product, process, organisation or evidence set is expected to fulfil.

data.title: Residual Risk
data.definition: The risk remaining after risk-control measures have been implemented and verified.

data.title: Responsibility Assignment
data.definition: A traceable allocation of a duty, decision right, review, approval or ownership obligation to an organisation, role or person.

data.title: Risk Control Measure
data.definition: A measure implemented to reduce risk, for example inherently safe design, protective measures or safety information. In the ontology it should normally be represented as RiskControlMeasure.

data.title: Risk Management Process
data.definition: The continuous lifecycle process for identifying hazards, estimating/evaluating risks, implementing and verifying controls, evaluating residual risk and updating the analysis from production and post-market information.

data.title: Risk Management
data.definition: The coordinated application of policies, procedures and practices to analyse, evaluate, control and monitor risk throughout the device lifecycle.

data.title: Risk
data.definition: The combination of the probability of occurrence of harm and the severity of that harm. In the ontology a risk should link to the relevant device configuration, hazardous situation, harms and controls.

data.title: Role
data.definition: A defined set of responsibilities and authority that may be assigned to a person or organisational function.

data.title: Rule
data.definition: A declared inference or decision rule that derives a conclusion from stated conditions while retaining its source and rationale.

data.title: Scientific Literature
data.definition: A published scientific source used as evidence or state-of-the-art input in clinical, risk or performance evaluation.

data.title: Sequence Of Events
data.definition: The ordered chain of events and conditions that can lead from a hazard to a hazardous situation and possible harm.

data.title: Serious Incident
data.definition: An incident that directly or indirectly led, might have led or might lead to death, serious deterioration in health, or a serious public-health threat, subject to the specific MDR criteria.

data.title: Shortage Risk
data.definition: The evaluated possibility and consequence of insufficient device supply for patients or healthcare systems.

data.title: Signal
data.definition: A new or changed indication arising from one or more data sources suggesting a potentially meaningful safety, performance or benefit-risk issue requiring assessment. Signal is useful operationally but should not be treated as though MDR Article 2 defines it as a standalone legal entity.

data.title: Software Change
data.definition: A controlled modification to software requirements, code, configuration, architecture, data or cybersecurity characteristics.

data.title: Software Version
data.definition: A controlled release/version of software incorporated in, forming part of, or itself constituting a device. It allows evidence, risk and configuration state to be tied to a precise software baseline.

data.title: Source Fragment
data.definition: A bounded, citable part of a source used to provide precise provenance for an ontology statement.

data.title: Source
data.definition: An identifiable origin of information used as provenance for a requirement, rule, assertion, decision or evidence item.

data.title: Source Update
data.definition: A new version, amendment or status change affecting a legal, guidance, standard, scientific or internal source.

data.title: SRN
data.definition: The Single Registration Number issued through EUDAMED to identify a registered economic operator.

data.title: SSCP
data.definition: The manufacturer-prepared summary of safety and clinical performance required for applicable implantable and Class III devices and validated by the notified body.

data.title: Standard Requirement
data.definition: A requirement or normative provision derived from a standard used by the manufacturer. It should retain provenance to the exact standard/version/clause and must not be confused with an MDR legal obligation.

data.title: Standard
data.definition: A document established by consensus and approved by a recognised body that provides rules, guidelines or characteristics for repeated use.

data.title: State Of The Art
data.definition: The generally acknowledged current level of technical and clinical development used as a benchmark for safety, performance and benefit-risk evaluation.

data.title: Submission
data.definition: A controlled package or transmission of regulatory information sent to an authority, notified body or regulatory information system.

data.title: Supplier Change
data.definition: A controlled modification involving a supplier, supplied item, outsourced process, site or supplier-control status.

data.title: Supplier Control Process
data.definition: The QMS process used to select, qualify, monitor and control suppliers and outsourced processes according to their risk and impact.

data.title: Supplier
data.definition: An external organisation providing a component, material, service or outsourced process used by the manufacturer. Manufacturer responsibility is not transferred merely because work is outsourced.

data.title: Supply Discontinuation
data.definition: The planned permanent cessation of supply of a device in a market or to affected customers.

data.title: Supply Forecast
data.definition: A time-based estimate of expected device availability, demand and potential supply constraints.

data.title: Supply Interruption
data.definition: An anticipated interruption in supply of certain devices that may fall within current MDR manufacturer notification obligations where the specified legal conditions are met. The ontology represents the event separately from the legal determination that notification is required.

data.title: Supply Status
data.definition: A controlled status describing current or anticipated device availability in a defined market and time period.

data.title: System
data.definition: A combination of interacting components or devices organised to perform a defined function in a product or operational context.

data.title: Target Population
data.definition: The patient or subject population for which the device is intended, characterized for example by age, condition, anatomy or other relevant clinical attributes.

data.title: Team Nb Guidance
data.definition: A non-binding position paper or guidance document issued by the European association of medical-device notified bodies.

data.title: Technical Documentation Set
data.definition: The manufacturer-controlled body of documentation described principally in MDR Annexes II and III demonstrating device design, manufacturing, safety, performance and post-market compliance. It is better represented as a structured set of evidence than as one file.

data.title: Test Report
data.definition: A controlled record describing a test method, test object/configuration, conditions, results, acceptance criteria and conclusion.

data.title: Traceability Record
data.definition: A record linking an identifier, product, organisation, transaction, submission or lifecycle event so its history and context can be reconstructed.

data.title: Training
data.definition: A planned activity that develops and records the competence needed to perform assigned work correctly.

data.title: Translation
data.definition: A controlled language version of manufacturer-supplied information, linked to its source version and review or approval state.

data.title: Trend
data.definition: A statistically or clinically significant increase in the frequency or severity of certain incidents or expected undesirable side-effects that may significantly affect benefit-risk and may trigger trend reporting.

data.title: UDI Di
data.definition: The **Device Identifier** portion of the UDI. It is specific to a manufacturer and a device or packaging level and is used to identify the particular device identity in the UDI system.

data.title: UDI Pi
data.definition: The **Production Identifier** portion of the UDI. It identifies production-related information such as lot, serial number, software identification or manufacturing/expiry information where applicable.

data.title: Use Case Demonstration
data.definition: A worked example showing how represented entities, relationships, rules and evidence answer a high-impact manufacturer use case.

data.title: Use Environment
data.definition: The physical and operational environment in which the device is intended to be used, such as hospital, ambulance, home, operating theatre or laboratory.

data.title: Use Limitation
data.definition: A condition or restriction that narrows where, how, by whom or for whom a device may be used safely and as intended.

data.title: Validation Evidence
data.definition: Evidence demonstrating that the resulting device, process or system is suitable for its intended use or intended purpose under applicable conditions.

data.title: Verification Evidence
data.definition: Evidence demonstrating that specified design or process outputs satisfy specified requirements — essentially, evidence that the implementation meets its specifications.

data.title: View
data.definition: A curated navigation or query page that presents ontology content for a particular task or perspective.

data.sequence: Evidence objective → scope → evidence set → quality → sufficiency → gaps/actions → update triggers → provenance.

data.title: AP-MARKET answer pattern
data.sequence: Route/status → prerequisites → notified-body implications → submissions → gate decision → date-sensitive provenance.

data.title: AP-PMS answer pattern
data.sequence: Trigger/data → assessment → decision → action/deadline → feedback → evidence → provenance.

data.title: AP-PROC answer pattern
data.sequence: Process/control → owner → inputs → activities → outputs → effectiveness/state → provenance.

data.title: AP-QUAL answer pattern
data.sequence: Conclusion → controlling product facts → applicable definitions → decision rationale → boundary or ambiguity → evidence → provenance → unresolved facts.

data.title: AP-REQ answer pattern
data.sequence: Applicable requirements → rationale → compliance method → risk/control → evidence → gap/status → provenance.

data.title: AP-TRACE answer pattern
data.sequence: Identity → duty → record state → responsibility → retention/synchronisation → provenance.
